what it holds: Stable identifier. Format: (UK|FR|EU)-[A-Z]{2,4}-nnn.
allowed values / notes: Cite this in prompt output so every decision is traceable to a row. Mnemonics: SCH scheduling, VIO violence, SEX sexual content, NUD nudity, LNG language, DRG drugs, IMI imitable behaviour, SUI suicide/self-harm, FLM film carry-over, MUS music videos, TRL trailers, SIG signage, CLS classification scheme, CV category V regime, PRO absolute prohibition, GEN general duty, DEF definition, LAW legal basis, SVC service scope, CNV channel convention, OCC occult, WEL participant welfare, OFF offence, FRM framework.

what it holds: Jurisdiction.
allowed values / notes: UK / FR / EU

what it holds: Body that issued the text.
allowed values / notes: Ofcom / Arcom / Parliament / EU-ERGA

what it holds: Nature of the source.
allowed values / notes: statute / regulator_binding / regulator_guidance / precedent / regulator_summary / classification_body / secondary

what it holds: Conflict resolution. LOWER WINS.
allowed values / notes: 1 statute, 2 regulator_binding, 3 guidance, 4 precedent, 5 regulator_summary, 6 classification_body, 7 secondary

what it holds: Whether a per-asset decision may rely on this row.
allowed values / notes: yes / definition_only / framework_only / pointer / scope_rule / no_out_of_scope

what it holds: Which services the rule binds. SEMICOLON-SEPARATED.
allowed values / notes: free_to_air, cinema_channels, pay_per_view, premium_subscription_film, other_than_cinema_channels, music_channels, bbc_odps, all_linear_tv, per_channel, pay_tv_bundles, all_avms

what it holds: Shared harm vocabulary across countries. THIS IS THE JOIN KEY to the content-extraction stage.
allowed values / notes: violence, sexual_content, nudity, drugs_alcohol_smoking, strong_language, fear_distress, suicide_self_harm, imitable_behaviour, human_dignity, occult_paranormal, religion, music_videos, trailers, film_carryover, signage, access_control, scheduling_general, classification_scheme, serious_harm, offence_general, participant_welfare, commercial_conditions, data_protection, legal_basis, definition, scope

what it holds: The age label or UK equivalent.
allowed values / notes: FR: I_tous_publics, II_-10, III_-12, IV_-16, V_-18. UK: context_dependent, watershed_bound, prohibited, any_time_with_protection, restricted_window. Also: category_independent, exempt, soft_restriction, n/a

what it holds: What the rule actually says, in structured prose.
allowed values / notes: Free text. Capitals mark the operative words.

what it holds: The time effect in words.
allowed values / notes: Free text.

what it holds: The time effect in a parseable form, for code. Semicolon-separated tokens.
allowed values / notes: none | prohibited | any_time | n/a | not_before=HH:MM | window=HH:MM-HH:MM | restricted_window=HH:MM-HH:MM | soft_prefer_not_before=HH:MM | not_within=... | not_near=... | not_when=... | prohibited_in=... | days=... | except_days=... | unless=... | requires=... | gate=... | override=... | annual_quota=... | sub_quota=... | standard=... | frequency_cap=... | exempt=... | see=RULE_ID | judgment:... | framework:...

what it holds: Carve-outs, gates and inputs the rule depends on.
allowed values / notes: Free text.

what it holds: PROPERTY OF THE RULE. Governs how the test set is scored.
allowed values / notes: bright_line = one correct answer, exact match required. conditional = bright line gated on an input; a correct missing-information request also passes. judgment_based = evaluative; score the reasoning and cited rule, accept a band, require escalation near thresholds.

what it holds: PROPERTY OF OUR EXTRACTION. Do NOT merge with determinacy.
allowed values / notes: clear / conflicting_sources / translation_uncertain / unverified / out_of_scope_for_asset_decision

what it holds: What is uncertain and how it was resolved.
allowed values / notes: Free text. Carries the C-0n conflict IDs.

what it holds: Escalate before relying on this row.
allowed values / notes: yes / no

what it holds: Source ID from the Sources tab.
allowed values / notes: e.g. UK-S1, FR-R1, EU-D1

what it holds: Clause within the source.
allowed values / notes: e.g. Rule 1.4, art. 3, AVMSD art. 6a(1)

what it holds: Canonical URL (hyperlinked).
allowed values / notes: PREFER A STABLE HTML PAGE over a PDF where the publisher offers one: an HTML page keeps its address across revisions, whereas PDF URLs are minted per revision (Ofcom /siteassets/ PDFs carry a ?v=NNNNNN parameter), so a pinned PDF link rots silently at the next update. For a row stating CURRENT law this is the CURRENT CONSOLIDATED text. The JORF/original-publication URL is cited only on superseded rows (9xx), where it is the correct source. Citing an original for current law is a provenance bug: it reads as authoritative while silently omitting later amendments.

what it holds: Date the provision took effect.
allowed values / notes: ISO date, or blank if undated guidance

what it holds: End of validity.
allowed values / notes: open / unknown / ISO date

what it holds: Fitness as ground truth.
allowed values / notes: approved = usable. draft = do not use until the conflict is resolved. unverified = currency unconfirmed. superseded = historical. NOTE: the manifest carries only CURRENT materials, so a superseded rule row would have no retrievable source; superseded wordings are recorded in the Open_Questions entry for the conflict that found them. A rule_id in the 9xx range is reserved for a historical version if one is ever carried again.

what it holds: Short quoted fragment that survived retrieval.
allowed values / notes: INCOMPLETE - see 99_EXTRACTION_NOTES. Cannot yet support an automated quote-integrity check because no local copy of the source exists.

what it holds: Language of the quote.
allowed values / notes: EN / FR

what it holds: Confidence in this extraction.
allowed values / notes: high / medium / low

what it holds: Date this row was last checked.
allowed values / notes: ISO date
